Suppose that $\mathcal{L}$ is $l$-local with interaction strength bounded by $s_{\mathcal{L}}$ and contains a bulk-dissipative cover $\mathfrak U$ with local mixing time $t_{\mathrm{loc}}$ in the displayed decomposition, and that $\mathcal{G}$ is $k$-local with interaction strength bounded by $s_{\mathcal{G}}$. Assume that $t_{\mathrm{loc}},a,\mathfrak d$ are bounded uniformly in the system size. We use the same cover to study $\mathcal{G}=\mathcal{L}+V$. Let $r:=\max\{l,k\}$ and define
\begin{align}
    s_V &:= \max_{x\in\Lambda} \sum_{B\ni x}||V_B||_{1\to1}.
\end{align}
Then
\begin{align}
    \kappa_{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathrm{loc}} &\leq\kappa_{\mathcal{L}}^{\sharp}+4a\mathfrak d\,r s_V. \label{eq:app-difference-sharp-load}
\end{align}
Moreover,
\begin{align}
    \kappa_{\mathcal{L}}^{\sharp} &\leq 4a\,s_{\mathcal{L},\mathfrak U}, & s_V &\leq s_{\mathcal{L}}+s_{\mathcal{G}}, \notag\\
    \kappa_{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathrm{loc}} &\leq4a\bigl(s_{\mathcal{L},\mathfrak U}+\mathfrak d\,r(s_{\mathcal{L}}+s_{\mathcal{G}})\bigr). && \label{eq:app-difference-coarse-load}
\end{align}
If
\begin{align}
    \kappa_{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathrm{loc}}t_{\mathrm{loc}}&\leq\frac12-\Delta,
\end{align}
for some $\Delta>0$ independent of the system size, then $(\mathcal{G}_N)_N$ has a unique fixed point at each size and is rapidly mixing with constant decay rate.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{cor:app-difference}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:app-difference} 

Since each local Lindbladian is trace-annihilating on its support,
\begin{align}
    V_B^*(\mathbb{I}_B\otimes O_{B^c}) &= \mathcal{G}_B^*(\mathbb{I}_B\otimes O_{B^c})-\mathcal{L}_B^*(\mathbb{I}_B\otimes O_{B^c})=0.
\end{align}
Thus $V$ is locally trace-annihilating. For every $\alpha$, the reference generator in \cref{eq:app-local-perturbation-reference-generator} is
\begin{align}
    \mathcal C_\alpha &= \sum_{\substack{B\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathcal S_{\mathcal{M}_\alpha}\\
    B\cap A_\alpha\neq\varnothing\\ [\mathcal{M}_\alpha,\mathcal{L}_B]
    =0}}\mathcal{L}_B+\sum_{\substack{B\in\mathcal S\\
    B\cap A_\alpha=\varnothing}}\mathcal{G}_B.
\end{align}
This is a Lindblad generator. Therefore \cref{lem:app-per-site-influence} gives \cref{eq:app-scalar-volterra} and \cref{eq:app-difference-sharp-load}. \cref{eq:app-local-perturbation-base-load} gives the bound on $\kappa_{\mathcal{L}}^{\sharp}$, while the triangle inequality gives
\begin{align}
    s_V &\leq \max_{x\in\Lambda}\sum_{B\ni x}\bigl(||\mathcal{G}_B||_{1\to1}+||\mathcal{L}_B||_{1\to1}\bigr)\leq s_{\mathcal{G}}+s_{\mathcal{L}}.
\end{align}
These two estimates give \cref{eq:app-difference-coarse-load}. The conclusion follows by applying \cref{lem:app-volterra-decay,lem:app-trace-oscillator} to \cref{eq:app-scalar-volterra} with the exact coefficient $\kappa_{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathrm{loc}}$. The assumed margin gives a decay rate at least $\Delta/(2t_{\mathrm{loc}})$ and a uniformly bounded Volterra prefactor. Since $M\leq\mathfrak d|\Lambda|$, the trace-norm prefactor grows at most linearly with the system size.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:app-perturbed-hamiltonians-jumps} 
  \addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{ 
    \texorpdfstring{\protect\cref*{cor:app-perturbed-hamiltonians-jumps}}{Result \getrefnumber{cor:app-perturbed-hamiltonians-jumps}}: Perturbation of Hamiltonians and jump operators} 

Consider the Lindbladian families $(\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,N})_N$, with $\mathcal{G}_\varepsilon=\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,N}$ at each size and
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{G}_\varepsilon(\rho) &:= -i[H_0+\varepsilon H_1,\rho] +\sum_{B,\mu} \mathcal D[L_{B,\mu,0}+\varepsilon L_{B,\mu,1}](\rho), \qquad H_j=\sum_Xh_{X,j},
\end{align}
where $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$, $\mu$ labels the different jump operators supported on $B$, $h_{X,j}=h_{X,j}^\dagger$ for $j=0,1$, and all displayed local terms have supports of size at most $r$. Let $\mathcal{L}:=\mathcal{G}_0$, with the local decomposition given by the displayed Hamiltonian terms and dissipators, and suppose that this decomposition contains a bulk-dissipative cover $\mathfrak U$ with local mixing time $t_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Assume that $t_{\mathrm{loc}},a,\mathfrak d$ are bounded uniformly in the system size. Define
\begin{align}
    s_1 &:= \max_{x\in\Lambda} \left( 2\sum_{X\ni x}||h_{X,1}|| +4\sum_{\substack{B\ni x\\
    \mu}} ||L_{B,\mu,0}||||L_{B,\mu,1}|| \right), \notag\\
    s_2 &:= 2\max_{x\in\Lambda} \sum_{\substack{B\ni x\\
    \mu}} ||L_{B,\mu,1}||^2.
\end{align}
The same cover is used for every $\varepsilon$, and \cref{eq:app-local-perturbation-base-load} gives $\kappa_{\mathcal{L}}^{\sharp}\leq4a\,s_{\mathcal{L},\mathfrak U}$. If
\begin{align}
    \bigl(\kappa_{\mathcal{L}}^{\sharp}+4a\mathfrak d\,r(|\varepsilon|s_1+\varepsilon^2s_2)\bigr)t_{\mathrm{loc}}&\leq\frac12-\Delta,
\end{align}
for some $\Delta>0$ independent of the system size, then $(\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,N})_N$ has a unique fixed point at each size and is rapidly mixing with constant decay rate. No tracelessness assumption on the jump operators is required.
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{cor:app-perturbed-hamiltonians-jumps}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:app-perturbed-hamiltonians-jumps} 

For operators $L_0,L_1$ supported on $B$, define
\begin{align}
    \mathcal C[L_0,L_1](\rho) &:= L_0\rho L_1^\dagger+L_1\rho L_0^\dagger-\frac12\{L_0^\dagger L_1+L_1^\dagger L_0,\rho\}.
\end{align}
Expanding the dissipator gives
\begin{align}
    \mathcal D[L_0+\varepsilon L_1] &= \mathcal D[L_0]+\varepsilon\mathcal C[L_0,L_1]+\varepsilon^2\mathcal D[L_1]. \label{eq:app-jump-expansion}
\end{align}
If $X=\mathbb{I}_B\otimes O_{B^c}$, then $X$ commutes with $L_0$ and $L_1$, and hence
\begin{align}
    \mathcal C[L_0,L_1]^*(X) &= L_0^\dagger XL_1+L_1^\dagger XL_0-\frac12\{L_0^\dagger L_1+L_1^\dagger L_0,X\}=0.
\end{align}
Thus the cross term is locally trace-annihilating. Moreover,
\begin{align}
    ||\mathcal C[L_0,L_1]||_{1\to1} &\leq 4||L_0||||L_1||, \notag\\
    ||\mathcal D[L_1]||_{1\to1} &\leq 2||L_1||^2, \notag\\
    ||-i[h,\,\cdot\,]||_{1\to1} &\leq 2||h||, \label{eq:app-jump-local-norms}
\end{align}
where the estimates follow from $||A\rho B||_1\leq||A||||B||||\rho||_1$ and the triangle inequality. It follows that $\mathcal{G}_\varepsilon-\mathcal{L}$ is locally trace-annihilating and has local interaction strength at most $|\varepsilon|s_1+\varepsilon^2s_2$.

Align the displayed Hamiltonian terms and dissipators, adding zero terms when necessary, and write
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{L} &= \sum_{B\in\mathcal S}\mathcal{L}_B, & \mathcal{G}_\varepsilon &= \sum_{B\in\mathcal S}\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,B}, & V_B&:=\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,B}-\mathcal{L}_B.
\end{align}
For every $\alpha$, the reference generator in \cref{eq:app-local-perturbation-reference-generator} is
\begin{align}
    \mathcal C_\alpha &= \sum_{\substack{B\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathcal S_{\mathcal{M}_\alpha}\\
    B\cap A_\alpha\neq\varnothing\\ [\mathcal{M}_\alpha,\mathcal{L}_B]
    =0}}\mathcal{L}_B+\sum_{\substack{B\in\mathcal S\\
    B\cap A_\alpha=\varnothing}}\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,B}.
\end{align}
Every term in this expression is a Lindblad generator. Hence \cref{lem:app-per-site-influence} gives $\kappa_{\mathcal{G}_\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{loc}}\leq \kappa_{\mathcal{L}}^{\sharp}+4a\mathfrak d\,r(|\varepsilon|s_1+\varepsilon^2s_2)$. The assumed margin and \cref{lem:app-volterra-decay,lem:app-trace-oscillator} give a decay rate at least $\Delta/(2t_{\mathrm{loc}})$ and a trace-norm prefactor of order $M\leq\mathfrak d|\Lambda|$, proving the stated uniform mixing bound. The calculation also shows directly that no tracelessness assumption is needed.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
\label{cor:app-rfa-gibbs-sampler-stability} 
  \addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{ 
    \texorpdfstring{\protect\cref*{cor:app-rfa-gibbs-sampler-stability}}{Result \getrefnumber{cor:app-rfa-gibbs-sampler-stability}}: Stability of the Gibbs sampler} 

Let $\Lambda$ be a $D$-dimensional lattice of qubits and let $H=\sum_Xh_X$ have finite interaction range and be $(k,l)$-local: each term acts on at most $k$ sites, and each site meets at most $l$ terms. Assume $||h_X||\leq h$, with the range and $D,h,k,l$ bounded uniformly in the system size. Write $\mathcal{L}^{(\beta)}=\mathcal{L}_N^{(\beta)}$ for the family $(\mathcal{L}_N^{(\beta)})_N$ of Gibbs samplers in \cite{RouzeFrancaAlhambra2024b} with single-qubit Pauli bath couplings. The infinite-temperature generator $\mathcal{L}^{(0)}$ contains the singleton bulk-dissipative cover $\mathfrak U_0$ defined in \cref{eq:app-rfa-bulk-cover}, with local mixing time $t_{\mathrm{loc}}^{(0)}=\sqrt{2}e^{1/4}\log4$ and $a=\mathfrak d=1$. There exists a size-independent $\beta_*>0$ such that, for every fixed locality $r$ and interaction-strength bound $s_{\mathcal{K}}$, there is a size-independent $\varepsilon_*>0$ with the following property: for every $r$-local Lindbladian family $(\mathcal{K}_N)_N$ with interaction strength at most $s_{\mathcal{K}}$, $(\mathcal{L}_N^{(\beta)}+\varepsilon\mathcal{K}_N)_N$ has a unique fixed point at each size and is rapidly mixing with constant decay rate whenever $0\leq\beta<\beta_*$ and $0\leq\varepsilon<\varepsilon_*$.
\label{eq:app-rfa-stability-radius}
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{cor:app-rfa-gibbs-sampler-stability}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:app-rfa-gibbs-sampler-stability} 

Write $\mathcal{K}=\mathcal{K}_N$ and define
\begin{align}
    \lambda_0 &:= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}e^{1/4}},\qquad t_{\mathrm{loc}}^{(0)}:=\lambda_0^{-1}\log4.
\end{align}
Define the cover
\begin{align}
    \mathfrak U_0 &:= \left\{\bigl(\{a\},\{a\},\mathcal{M}_a\bigr):a\in\Lambda\right\}, & \mathcal{M}_a^*(O) &:= \lambda_0\left(\frac12\mathbb{I}_a\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_a(O)-O\right). \label{eq:app-rfa-bulk-cover}
\end{align}

We first verify that $\mathfrak U_0$ is a bulk-dissipative cover with local mixing time $t_{\mathrm{loc}}^{(0)}$ and that $\mathcal{L}^{(0)}$ contains it. Using $ \mathcal R_a(O) := \frac12\mathbb{I}_a\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_a(O), \mathcal{M}_a^* = \lambda_0(\mathcal R_a-\operatorname{id})$, at infinite temperature we have
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{L}^{(0)} &= \sum_{a\in\Lambda}\mathcal{M}_a.
\end{align}
The asymptotic projection of $\mathcal{M}_a^*$ is $P_{\mathcal{M}_a}^*=\mathcal R_a$, and
\begin{align}
    e^{t\mathcal{M}_a^*}-P_{\mathcal{M}_a}^* &=e^{-\lambda_0t}\left(\operatorname{id}-\mathcal R_a\right).
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
    ||e^{t\mathcal{M}_a}-P_{\mathcal{M}_a}||_\diamond &\leq2e^{-\lambda_0t}.
\end{align}
Moreover,
\begin{align}
    \ker\mathcal{M}_a^* &=\mathbb{I}_a\otimes\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{a^c}).
\end{align}
At $t=t_{\mathrm{loc}}^{(0)}$, this diamond-norm bound is at most $1/2$. The regions $A_a=A_a^\circ=\{a\}$ cover the lattice, each $\mathcal{M}_a$ is a term of $\mathcal{L}^{(0)}$, and their size and incidence are both one. Hence $\mathfrak U_0$ is the asserted bulk-dissipative cover and $\mathcal{L}^{(0)}$ contains it.

Let $\kappa_\beta$ denote the size-independent coefficient in the commutator and diagonal-difference bounds below. We now combine the commutator estimate of \cite[Appendix~B.1]{RouzeFrancaAlhambra2024b} with the local perturbation estimate. Write $\mathcal{L}^{(\beta)}=\sum_b\mathcal{L}_b^{(\beta)}$, where each bath-site term $\mathcal{L}_b^{(\beta)}$ is a Lindbladian, and put $\delta_a=\operatorname{id}-\mathcal R_a$. Define
\begin{align}
    \mathcal F_a^{(\beta)} &:=\delta_a((\mathcal{L}_a^{(\beta)})^*-\mathcal{M}_a^*) +\sum_{b\neq a}[\delta_a,(\mathcal{L}_b^{(\beta)})^*].
\end{align}
In this work \cite[Eq.~(25)]{RouzeFrancaAlhambra2024b}, the commutators and the diagonal difference are bounded separately. Summing those estimates gives, for every observable $O$,
\begin{align}
    \sum_a||\mathcal F_a^{(\beta)}(O)|| &\leq\kappa_\beta\sum_c||\delta_c O||. \label{eq:app-rfa-source-bound}
\end{align}
For the perturbation, the singleton reset telescope used in \cref{lem:app-per-site-influence} gives
\begin{align}
    \sum_a\left\|\sum_{B:a\in B}\delta_a\mathcal{K}_B^*(O)\right\| &\overset{(1)}{\leq}4\sum_B |B|\,||\mathcal{K}_B||_{1\to1}\sum_{c\in B}||\delta_c O||,\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{\leq}4rs_{\mathcal{K}}\sum_c||\delta_c O||, \label{eq:app-rfa-local-bound}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ uses $\mathcal{K}_B^*(\mathbb{I})=0$, $||\delta_a||\leq2$, and the reset telescoping sum \cref{eq:app-reset-telescope} on $B$, and $(2)$ exchanges the sums and uses $|B|\leq r$ and $\sum_{B\ni c}||\mathcal{K}_B||_{1\to1}\leq s_{\mathcal{K}}$.
Set $\mathcal{G}:=\mathcal{L}^{(\beta)}+\varepsilon\mathcal{K}$ and $O_t:=e^{t\mathcal{G}^*}(O)$. For each site $a$, define the Lindblad generator
\begin{align}
    \mathcal C_a&:=\sum_{b\neq a}\mathcal{L}_b^{(\beta)}+\varepsilon\sum_{B:a\notin B}\mathcal{K}_B.
\end{align}
Differentiating and grouping the terms gives
\begin{align}
    \frac{d}{dt}(\delta_a O_t)
    &=\delta_a\bigl((\mathcal{L}^{(\beta)})^*+\varepsilon\mathcal{K}^*\bigr)(O_t),\notag\\
    &\overset{(1)}{=}\left(\sum_{b\neq a}(\mathcal{L}_b^{(\beta)})^*-\lambda_0\operatorname{id}\right)(\delta_a O_t)
      +\mathcal F_a^{(\beta)}(O_t)
      +\varepsilon\sum_{B:a\notin B}\mathcal{K}_B^*(\delta_a O_t)
      +\varepsilon\sum_{B:a\in B}\delta_a\mathcal{K}_B^*(O_t),\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{=}(\mathcal C_a^*-\lambda_0\operatorname{id})(\delta_a O_t)
      +\mathcal F_a^{(\beta)}(O_t)
      +\varepsilon\sum_{B:a\in B}\delta_a\mathcal{K}_B^*(O_t). \label{eq:app-rfa-damped-source}
\end{align}
Here $(1)$ uses $\delta_a(\mathcal{L}_b^{(\beta)})^*=(\mathcal{L}_b^{(\beta)})^*\delta_a+[\delta_a,(\mathcal{L}_b^{(\beta)})^*]$, $\delta_a\mathcal{M}_a^*=-\lambda_0\delta_a$, and the definition of $\mathcal F_a^{(\beta)}$; perturbation terms supported away from $a$ commute with $\delta_a$. Step $(2)$ is the definition of $\mathcal C_a$.
The scalar damping commutes with $\mathcal C_a^*$, whose semigroup is a unital contraction. Integrating \cref{eq:app-rfa-damped-source} gives
\begin{align}
    \delta_a O_t
    &=e^{-\lambda_0t}e^{t\mathcal C_a^*}\delta_a O
      +\int_0^t e^{-\lambda_0(t-s)}e^{(t-s)\mathcal C_a^*}
      \left(\mathcal F_a^{(\beta)}(O_s)
      +\varepsilon\sum_{B:a\in B}\delta_a\mathcal{K}_B^*(O_s)\right)ds.
\end{align}
Taking norms, summing over $a$, and using \cref{eq:app-rfa-source-bound,eq:app-rfa-local-bound}, we obtain, for $S(t):=\sum_a\|\delta_a O_t\|$ and $b:=\kappa_\beta+4\varepsilon r s_{\mathcal{K}}$,
\begin{align}
    S(t)&\leq e^{-\lambda_0t}S(0)+b\int_0^t e^{-\lambda_0(t-s)}S(s)\,ds. \label{eq:app-rfa-volterra}
\end{align}
A sufficient condition for a positive decay rate is
\begin{align}
    \left(\kappa_\beta+4\varepsilon r s_{\mathcal{K}}\right)t_{\mathrm{loc}}^{(0)} &<\frac12. \label{eq:app-rfa-stability-condition}
\end{align}
Since $e^{-\lambda_0t}\leq2^{-\lfloor t/t_{\mathrm{loc}}^{(0)}\rfloor}$, \cref{lem:app-volterra-decay} applies under \cref{eq:app-rfa-stability-condition}. Combining its oscillator decay with \cref{lem:app-trace-oscillator}, for the reset cover $\mathfrak U_0$ with $M=|\Lambda|$, proves uniqueness and the stated mixing bound. For fixed $\beta,r,s_{\mathcal{K}},\varepsilon$ satisfying \cref{eq:app-rfa-stability-condition}, the coefficient $b$ and the local mixing time are uniform in the system size, so the decay rate is constant.

The high-temperature estimates of \cite{RouzeFrancaAlhambra2024b} give $\beta_*>0$ and a uniform margin $\Delta>0$ such that $\kappa_\beta t_{\mathrm{loc}}^{(0)}\leq1/2-\Delta$ for $0\leq\beta<\beta_*$. Choosing $\varepsilon_*>0$ so that $4\varepsilon_*r s_{\mathcal{K}}t_{\mathrm{loc}}^{(0)}\leq\Delta/2$ retains a uniform positive margin in \cref{eq:app-rfa-stability-condition}, proving the corollary and \cref{cor:main-gibbs-stability}.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- corollary-9: body_md -->
\label{cor:app-mpdo-parent-stability} 
  \addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{ 
    \texorpdfstring{\protect\cref*{cor:app-mpdo-parent-stability}}{Result \getrefnumber{cor:app-mpdo-parent-stability}}: Stability of simple injective MPDO parent Lindbladians} 

Consider the parent Lindbladian family $(\mathcal{L}_N)_N$ of the simple injective renormalization-fixed-point construction in \cite[Theorem~III.9 and Section~V~A]{liu2026parent}, on a periodic chain of $N\geq5$ sites. Fix the local tensor data independently of $N$, with sites understood after any fixed blocking. Work on the complete canonical physical space with positive sector weights $a_u b_v>0$. Each $\mathcal{L}_N$ contains the three-site bulk-dissipative cover $\mathfrak U_{\mathrm{MPDO}}$ defined in \cref{eq:app-mpdo-cover}, with local mixing time $t_{\mathrm{loc}}=\log4$ and $a=\mathfrak d=3$. For every fixed locality $k$ and per-site interaction-strength bound $s_{\mathcal{K}}$, there is a size-independent $\varepsilon_*>0$ such that, for every $k$-local Lindbladian family $(\mathcal{K}_N)_N$ with interaction strength at most $s_{\mathcal{K}}$, $(\mathcal{L}_N+\varepsilon\mathcal{K}_N)_N$ has a unique stationary state at each size and is rapidly mixing with constant decay rate for all $0\leq\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_*$. At $\varepsilon=0$, the stationary state is the specified MPDO.
<!-- end corollary-9 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{cor:app-mpdo-parent-stability}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:app-mpdo-parent-stability} 

The complete canonical physical space and bond data are
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{H}&=\bigoplus_u\bigl(\mathcal{H}_l^{(u)}\otimes\mathcal{H}_r^{(u)}\bigr), \qquad \eta_{u,v}\succeq0,\qquad \operatorname{Tr}\eta_{u,v}=a_u b_v,\qquad \sum_u a_u b_u=1, \label{eq:app-mpdo-canonical-data}
\end{align}
where $\eta_{u,v}$ acts on $\mathcal{H}_r^{(u)}\otimes\mathcal{H}_l^{(v)}$. Let $\mathcal E_i$ be the three-site channel of Eq.~(55) of that reference, translated to sites $i,i+1,i+2$, with indices taken modulo $N$, and set
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_N&=\sum_{i=1}^N\mathcal{L}_i,\qquad \mathcal{L}_i=\mathcal E_i-\operatorname{id}.
\end{align}
Define
\begin{align}
    \mathfrak U_{\mathrm{MPDO}} &:=\left\{\bigl(A_i^\circ,\{i,i+1,i+2\},\mathcal{L}_i\bigr):i=1,\ldots,N\right\} \label{eq:app-mpdo-cover}
\end{align}
and verify below that it is a bulk-dissipative cover with local mixing time $t_{\mathrm{loc}}=\log4$ and $a=\mathfrak d=3$, contained in $\mathcal{L}$. Here $A_i^\circ$ is the bulk of $\mathcal{L}_i$ defined in \cref{eq:app-bulk-dissipation}; it contains the middle site $i+1$.

We verify the cover hypotheses and apply the local-mixing-time criterion. On a patch of sites $1,2,3$, define the sector maps $Q_u:\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}_l^{(u)}\otimes\mathcal{H}_r^{(u)}$ by
\begin{align*}
    Q_u\left(\bigoplus_v\psi_v\right)&:=\psi_u,\qquad \psi_v\in\mathcal{H}_l^{(v)}\otimes\mathcal{H}_r^{(v)}.
\end{align*}
They satisfy $Q_uQ_v^\dagger=0$ for $u\neq v$, $Q_uQ_u^\dagger=\mathbb{I}_{\mathcal{H}_l^{(u)}\otimes\mathcal{H}_r^{(u)}}$, and $\sum_uQ_u^\dagger Q_u=\mathbb{I}_\mathcal{H}$. Set
\begin{align}
    R_{u,v}(X) &:=\operatorname{Tr}_{1r,2,3l}\!\left[(Q_u\otimes\mathbb{I}_2\otimes Q_v)X(Q_u^\dagger\otimes\mathbb{I}_2\otimes Q_v^\dagger)\right],\notag\\
    \Omega_{u,v}&:=\bigoplus_w\bigl(\eta_{u,w}\otimes\eta_{w,v}\bigr). \label{eq:app-mpdo-channel-factors}
\end{align}
The channel of Eq.~(55) of \cite{liu2026parent} is
\begin{align}
    \mathcal E(X)&=\bigoplus_{u,v}\left[R_{u,v}(X)\otimes\frac{\Omega_{u,v}}{a_u b_v}\right], \label{eq:app-mpdo-channel}
\end{align}
with tensor factors placed in physical order: $R_{u,v}$ retains $1l,3r$, while $\Omega_{u,v}$ occupies $1r,2,3l$. The bond normalization gives
\begin{align}
    \operatorname{Tr}\Omega_{u,v} &\overset{(1)}{=}\sum_w(a_u b_w)(a_w b_v) \overset{(2)}{=}a_u b_v, \label{eq:app-mpdo-channel-normalization}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ uses the bond traces and $(2)$ uses $\sum_w a_w b_w=1$. Thus the channel measures the complete outer-sector decomposition, traces the selected factors, and inserts a normalized state. Orthogonality of the sectors then gives
\begin{align}
    R_{u,v}(\mathcal E(X))&=R_{u,v}(X)\frac{\operatorname{Tr}\Omega_{u,v}}{a_u b_v}=R_{u,v}(X), \qquad \mathcal E^2(X)=\mathcal E(X). \label{eq:app-mpdo-idempotence}
\end{align}
Consequently,
\begin{align}
    e^{t\mathcal{L}_i}&=\mathcal E_i+e^{-t}(\operatorname{id}-\mathcal E_i),\notag\\
    \|e^{t\mathcal{L}_i}-\mathcal E_i\|_\diamond&\leq2e^{-t}. \label{eq:app-mpdo-local-decay}
\end{align}
Each $\mathcal{L}_i$ is a Lindbladian: if $F_\nu$ are Kraus operators of $\mathcal E_i$, their completeness relation gives $\mathcal E_i-\operatorname{id}=\sum_\nu\mathcal D[F_\nu]$.

Since the sector maps act only on the outer sites, $R_{u,v}(X)$ depends on $X$ only through $\operatorname{Tr}_2X$. Hence $\mathcal E=\Phi\circ\operatorname{Tr}_2$, where $\Phi$ performs the same outer-sector measurement and normalized-state insertion. Taking adjoints gives
\begin{align}
    \ker(\mathcal E^*-\operatorname{id}) &\overset{(1)}{=}\operatorname{Ran}\mathcal E^* \overset{(2)}{\subseteq}\mathbb{I}_2\otimes\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\{1,3\}}), \label{eq:app-mpdo-bulk-erasure}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ uses idempotence and $(2)$ uses that $(\operatorname{Tr}_2)^*$ inserts the identity at site $2$. This proves the bulk condition for the entire middle site, including its sector label, and remains true after tensoring with the identity outside the patch.

At $t=\log4$, \cref{eq:app-mpdo-local-decay} is at most $1/2$. Since $i+1\in A_i^\circ$ for every $i$, the bulk regions cover the chain. Each enlarged region has three sites, and each site belongs to three enlarged regions. Thus \cref{eq:app-mpdo-local-decay,eq:app-mpdo-bulk-erasure} give the claimed cover, with $M=N$, $t_{\mathrm{loc}}=\log4$, and $a=\mathfrak d=3$. The local terms commute by Section~V~A, Eqs.~(57)--(58), of \cite{liu2026parent}; triples sharing only one endpoint act on its opposite left and right factors within the same diagonal sector.
Write $\mathcal{K}=\mathcal{K}_N$. For every perturbation term $\mathcal{K}_B$, $n_{\mathfrak U_{\mathrm{MPDO}}}(B)\leq\mathfrak d|B|\leq3k$, and hence $s_{\mathcal{K},\mathfrak U_{\mathrm{MPDO}}}\leq3ks_{\mathcal{K}}$. The commuting incoming influence therefore satisfies
\begin{align}
    \kappa_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{com}}\leq4a\varepsilon s_{\mathcal{K},\mathfrak U_{\mathrm{MPDO}}}&\leq36\varepsilon k s_{\mathcal{K}}.
\end{align}
A sufficient condition is therefore
\begin{align}
    36\varepsilon k s_{\mathcal{K}}\,t_{\mathrm{loc}}&<\frac12,\qquad t_{\mathrm{loc}}=\log4. \label{eq:app-mpdo-stability-condition}
\end{align}
This implies $\kappa_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{com}}t_{\mathrm{loc}}<1/2$, and \cref{cor:commuting-strong-bulk-dissipation} proves uniqueness and rapid mixing with constant decay rate. At $\varepsilon=0$, the parent construction fixes the specified MPDO, which is therefore the unique stationary state. For fixed $k$ and $s_{\mathcal{K}}>0$, choose $\varepsilon_*=(144k s_{\mathcal{K}}\log4)^{-1}$. Then the left-hand side of \cref{eq:app-mpdo-stability-condition} is at most $1/4$ for every permitted perturbation and every $0\leq\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_*$. When $s_{\mathcal{K}}=0$, the perturbation vanishes and any positive threshold works. This proves the corollary and \cref{cor:main-mpdo-stability}.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{cor:main-local-noise}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:main-local-noise} 

Let $\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_N=\sum_B\mathcal{L}_B$ be a geometrically local Lindbladian on the fixed-dimensional lattice, with $\zeta(\mathcal{L})=\max_x\sum_{B\ni x}|B|\,\|\mathcal{L}_B\|_{1\to1}$ bounded independently of the system size. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathcal{N}}$ be a family of bounded, possibly overlapping regions of size at most $a$ that cover the lattice, with each site contained in at most $\mathfrak d$ regions, and write $\mathcal{N}=\mathcal{N}_N=\sum_{B\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal{N}}}\mathcal{N}_B$. Assume that $\mathcal{N}$ is geometrically local and has uniformly bounded per-site interaction strength. The setting is illustrated in \cref{fig:local-noise-obstructs-order}a). Each $\mathcal{N}_B$ may be any locally relaxing Lindbladian with a unique stationary state on its support $B$. Thus its whole support is a bulk. Suppose uniformly in $B$ that
\begin{align}
    \left\lVert e^{t_{\mathrm{noise}}\mathcal{N}_B}-P_{\mathcal{N}_B}\right\rVert_\diamond&\leq\frac12.
\end{align}
Let $\kappa_{\mathcal{N}}^{\sharp}$ be the reference coefficient in \cref{eq:app-bulk-incoming-L}, with $\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{N}$ and this noise cover. Thus it is the same refinement as $\kappa_{\mathcal{L}}^{\sharp}$, and \cref{eq:app-sharp-main-comparison} gives $\kappa_{\mathcal{N}}^{\sharp}\leq\kappa_{\mathcal{N}}$, where $\kappa_{\mathcal{N}}$ is the main-text coefficient. Consequently, the main-text assumption implies $1/2-\kappa_{\mathcal{N}}^{\sharp}t_{\mathrm{noise}}\geq\Delta>0$. Scaling the noise by $\varepsilon$ changes this rate to $\varepsilon\kappa_{\mathcal{N}}^{\sharp}$ and the local mixing time to $t_{\mathrm{noise}}/\varepsilon$. Let $\Delta_{\mathcal{N}}:=1/2-\kappa_{\mathcal{N}}^{\sharp}t_{\mathrm{noise}}$.
By \cref{lem:app-per-site-influence}, the bound $\kappa_{\mathcal{L}+\varepsilon\mathcal{N}}^{\mathrm{loc}}\leq\varepsilon\kappa_{\mathcal{N}}^{\sharp}+4a\mathfrak d\,\zeta(\mathcal{L})$ shows that, if $\Delta_{\mathcal{N}}>0$, the sum $\mathcal{L}+\varepsilon\mathcal{N}$ is rapidly mixing whenever
\begin{align}
    \varepsilon&>\frac{4a\mathfrak d\,\zeta(\mathcal{L})t_{\mathrm{noise}}}{\Delta_{\mathcal{N}}}. \label{eq:local-noise-order-threshold}
\end{align}
For a $k$-local $\mathcal{L}$ with interaction strength bounded by $s_{\mathcal{L}}$, one may use $\zeta(\mathcal{L})\leq k s_{\mathcal{L}}$. If the $\mathcal{N}_B$ commute, then $\kappa_{\mathcal{N}}^{\sharp}=0$, so the mixing estimate imposes no additional smallness condition on the interaction strength of $\mathcal{N}$, and a sufficient condition becomes
\begin{align}
    \varepsilon&>8a\mathfrak d\,\zeta(\mathcal{L})t_{\mathrm{noise}}. \label{eq:commuting-local-noise-order-threshold}
\end{align}
To obtain a single threshold for the main-text family, choose uniform upper bounds $Z\geq\zeta(\mathcal{L}_N)$ and $T\geq t_{\mathrm{noise}}$, and take $\varepsilon_*:=4a\mathfrak d ZT/\Delta$. Every fixed $\varepsilon>\varepsilon_*$ leaves a margin at least $\Delta(1-\varepsilon_*/\varepsilon)>0$. The cover has $M=O(|\Lambda|)$ and local mixing time $O(1)$, proving the corollary and giving the rapid relaxation illustrated in \cref{fig:local-noise-obstructs-order}b).

For every fixed $\varepsilon$, $\mathcal{L}_N+\varepsilon\mathcal{N}_N$ is geometrically local with uniformly bounded per-site interaction strength. Preparing a state with nonvanishing connected correlations between bounded-support observables separated by distance $R$ from a product state requires time $\Omega(R)$ at sufficiently small fixed trace-norm error \cite{BravyiHastingsVerstraete2006,Poulin2010}. The same lower bound holds for topological target states covered by \cite{KoenigPastawski2014}, with separation scale $R$. For $R$ proportional to the lattice diameter, these bounds are incompatible with the $O(\log|\Lambda|)$ preparation time supplied by rapid mixing on a fixed-dimensional lattice.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
The Lindbladian
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{L}(\rho)=-i[H,\rho]+\sum_\mu\left(2L_\mu\rho L_\mu^\dagger-\{L_\mu^\dagger L_\mu,\rho\}\right)
\end{align*}
is called \emph{quasifree} if $H$ is quadratic in the Majorana operators and $L_\mu$ are linear:
\begin{align*}
    H=\frac{i}{4}\sum_{j,k=1}^m \mathbf{H}_{j,k}c_jc_k,\qquad L_\mu=\sum_{j=1}^m l_{\mu,j}c_j,
\end{align*}
where $\mathbf{H}=-\mathbf{H}^T\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:qf-adjoint-identities}
Let $\mathcal{L}^*$ be the Hilbert--Schmidt adjoint of $\mathcal{L}$. For every operator $O\in \mathcal{A}_m$,
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{L}^*(O)&=\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{i,j}\widetilde c_i\delta_jO+\sum_{i,j=1}^m(\mathbf{H}_{i,j}+4\mathbf{M}_{i,j})\delta_i\delta_jO, \label{eq:qf_adjoint_quasiderivations}\\
    \delta_i\mathcal{L}^* O&=\mathcal{L}^*\delta_iO+\sum_{r=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{i,r}\delta_rO. \label{eq:one_quasiderivation}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{lem:qf-adjoint-identities}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:qf-adjoint-identities} 

We first prove \cref{eq:qf_adjoint_quasiderivations} for an operator $O$ of parity $p\in\{+1,-1\}$. \cref{eq:dk_commutators} gives
\begin{align}
    O\widetilde c_j=p\widetilde c_jO-2p\delta_jO. \label{eq:right_mult_parity}
\end{align}
Since $\delta_i$ removes one Majorana factor, $\delta_iO$ has parity $-p$. The relation $\delta_j\delta_i=-\delta_i\delta_j$ follows directly from \cref{eq:qf-quasiderivation-definition}: when both distinct labels occur, removing the earlier factor shifts the position of the later one by one, reversing the sign between the two orders. If either label is absent, or the labels agree, both compositions vanish. Applying \cref{eq:right_mult_parity} to $\delta_iO$ therefore yields
\begin{align}
    (\delta_iO)\widetilde c_j&\overset{(1)}{=}-p\widetilde c_j\delta_iO+2p\delta_j\delta_iO,\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{=}-p\widetilde c_j\delta_iO-2p\delta_i\delta_jO, \label{eq:right_mult_derivative}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ uses its parity $-p$ and $(2)$ uses anticommutation of the quasiderivations. Using these two identities, we obtain
\begin{align}
    O\widetilde c_i\widetilde c_j&\overset{(1)}{=}(p\widetilde c_iO-2p\delta_iO)\widetilde c_j,\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{=}p\widetilde c_i(p\widetilde c_jO-2p\delta_jO)-2p(-p\widetilde c_j\delta_iO-2p\delta_i\delta_jO),\notag\\
    &\overset{(3)}{=}\widetilde c_i\widetilde c_jO-2\widetilde c_i\delta_jO+2\widetilde c_j\delta_iO+4\delta_i\delta_jO, \label{eq:qf-right-quadratic}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ uses \cref{eq:right_mult_parity}, $(2)$ uses \cref{eq:right_mult_parity} and \cref{eq:right_mult_derivative}, and $(3)$ expands and uses $p^2=1$. Subtracting \cref{eq:qf-right-quadratic} from $\widetilde c_i\widetilde c_jO$ gives
\begin{align}
    [\widetilde c_i\widetilde c_j,O]=2\widetilde c_i\delta_jO-2\widetilde c_j\delta_iO-4\delta_i\delta_jO. \label{eq:quadratic_commutator}
\end{align}
Since $\widetilde c_i \widetilde c_j = c_i c_j$, the Hamiltonian has the same coefficients in the dressed Majoranas. Consequently,
\begin{align}
    i[H,O]&\overset{(1)}{=}-\frac14\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{H}_{i,j}[\widetilde c_i\widetilde c_j,O],\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{=}-\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{H}_{i,j}\widetilde c_i\delta_jO+\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{H}_{i,j}\widetilde c_j\delta_iO+\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{H}_{i,j}\delta_i\delta_jO,\notag\\
    &\overset{(3)}{=}-\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{H}_{i,j}\widetilde c_i\delta_jO+\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{H}_{i,j}\delta_i\delta_jO, \label{eq:hamiltonian_quasiderivations}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ substitutes the Hamiltonian, $(2)$ uses \cref{eq:quadratic_commutator}, and $(3)$ exchanges $i,j$ in the second sum and uses $\mathbf{H}_{j,i}=-\mathbf{H}_{i,j}$.

We next consider the dissipative part. Since $\widetilde c_i = i\Pi c_i$ and $\Pi O\Pi=pO$, moving $\Pi$ through $\widetilde c_i$ gives
\begin{align}
    p\widetilde c_iO\widetilde c_j=c_iOc_j,\qquad c_ic_j=\widetilde c_i\widetilde c_j. \label{eq:qf-recycling-parity}
\end{align}
\cref{eq:right_mult_parity} also gives $p\widetilde c_iO\widetilde c_j=\widetilde c_i\widetilde c_jO-2\widetilde c_i\delta_jO$. Thus
\begin{align}
    2p\widetilde c_iO\widetilde c_j-\{\widetilde c_i\widetilde c_j,O\} &\overset{(1)}{=}2\widetilde c_i\widetilde c_jO-4\widetilde c_i\delta_jO-\widetilde c_i\widetilde c_jO-O\widetilde c_i\widetilde c_j,\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{=}-2\widetilde c_i\delta_jO-2\widetilde c_j\delta_iO-4\delta_i\delta_jO, \label{eq:dissipator_quasiderivations}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ uses the preceding identity and expands the anticommutator, and $(2)$ substitutes \cref{eq:qf-right-quadratic} and collects terms. Note that the right hand side does not depend on the parity $p$, so we can use it for an operator $O$ of either parity. Since $\mathbf{M}_{i,j}=\sum_\mu l_{\mu,i}l_{\mu,j}^*$, we obtain
\begin{align}
    \sum_\mu\left(2L_\mu^\dagger OL_\mu-\{L_\mu^\dagger L_\mu,O\}\right) &\overset{(1)}{=}\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{M}_{j,i}\left(2p\widetilde c_iO\widetilde c_j-\{\widetilde c_i\widetilde c_j,O\}\right),\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{=}-2\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{M}_{j,i}\widetilde c_i\delta_jO-2\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{M}_{j,i}\widetilde c_j\delta_iO-4\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{M}_{j,i}\delta_i\delta_jO,\notag\\
    &\overset{(3)}{=}-2\sum_{i,j=1}^m(\mathbf{M}_{i,j}+\mathbf{M}_{j,i})\widetilde c_i\delta_jO+4\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{M}_{i,j}\delta_i\delta_jO, \label{eq:dissipative_part_quasiderivations}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ expands the jumps and uses \cref{eq:qf-recycling-parity}, $(2)$ uses \cref{eq:dissipator_quasiderivations}, and $(3)$ exchanges $i,j$ in the second and third sums and uses $\delta_j\delta_i=-\delta_i\delta_j$. Adding \cref{eq:hamiltonian_quasiderivations} and \cref{eq:dissipative_part_quasiderivations} gives
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{L}^*(O)&\overset{(1)}{=}-\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{H}_{i,j}\widetilde c_i\delta_jO+\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{H}_{i,j}\delta_i\delta_jO-2\sum_{i,j=1}^m(\mathbf{M}_{i,j}+\mathbf{M}_{j,i})\widetilde c_i\delta_jO+4\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{M}_{i,j}\delta_i\delta_jO,\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{=}-\sum_{i,j=1}^m\bigl(\mathbf{H}_{i,j}+2\mathbf{M}_{i,j}+2\mathbf{M}_{j,i}\bigr)\widetilde c_i\delta_jO+\sum_{i,j=1}^m(\mathbf{H}_{i,j}+4\mathbf{M}_{i,j})\delta_i\delta_jO,\notag\\
    &\overset{(3)}{=}\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{i,j}\widetilde c_i\delta_jO+\sum_{i,j=1}^m(\mathbf{H}_{i,j}+4\mathbf{M}_{i,j})\delta_i\delta_jO, \label{eq:qf_adjoint_quasiderivations_derived}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ substitutes \cref{eq:hamiltonian_quasiderivations} into $i[H,O]$ and \cref{eq:dissipative_part_quasiderivations} into the dissipative part, $(2)$ collects the two first-order sums, and $(3)$ uses $\mathbf{X}_{i,j}=-\mathbf{H}_{i,j}-2(\mathbf{M}_{i,j}+\mathbf{M}_{j,i})$ from \cref{app:eq:quasifree_X}. This is \cref{eq:qf_adjoint_quasiderivations} on each parity sector, hence on every operator by linearity.

We now derive the second identity. Directly from \cref{eq:qf-quasiderivation-definition},
\begin{align}
    \delta_i\delta_j=-\delta_j\delta_i,\qquad \delta_i(\widetilde c_pO)=\delta_{i,p}O-\widetilde c_p\delta_iO, \label{eq:delta_relations}
\end{align}
where in the second equation we used that moving $\delta_i$ past the first factor contributes the minus sign, with the additional term $O$ when $i=p$. Applying \cref{eq:delta_relations} to \cref{eq:qf_adjoint_quasiderivations_derived} gives
\begin{align}
    \delta_i\mathcal{L}^* O&\overset{(1)}{=}\sum_{p,q=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{p,q}\delta_i(\widetilde c_p\delta_qO)+\sum_{p,q=1}^m(\mathbf{H}_{p,q}+4\mathbf{M}_{p,q})\delta_i\delta_p\delta_qO,\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{=}\sum_{q=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{i,q}\delta_qO+\sum_{p,q=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{p,q}\widetilde c_p\delta_q\delta_iO+\sum_{p,q=1}^m(\mathbf{H}_{p,q}+4\mathbf{M}_{p,q})\delta_p\delta_q\delta_iO,\notag\\
    &\overset{(3)}{=}\mathcal{L}^*\delta_iO+\sum_{q=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{i,q}\delta_qO, \notag
\end{align}
where $(1)$ substitutes \cref{eq:qf_adjoint_quasiderivations_derived}, $(2)$ uses both relations in \cref{eq:delta_relations}, and $(3)$ applies \cref{eq:qf_adjoint_quasiderivations_derived} to $\delta_iO$, which is allowed because that identity holds on both parity sectors. We have therefore proved, for every $O$,
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{L}^*(O)&=\sum_{i,j=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{i,j}\widetilde c_i\delta_jO+\sum_{i,j=1}^m(\mathbf{H}_{i,j}+4\mathbf{M}_{i,j})\delta_i\delta_jO,\\
    \delta_i\mathcal{L}^* O&=\mathcal{L}^*\delta_iO+\sum_{r=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{i,r}\delta_rO.
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:qf-closed-evolution}
Let $T_t=e^{t\mathcal{L}^*}$. For every operator $O\in \mathcal{A}_m$,
\begin{align}
    \delta_iT_tO=\sum_{p=1}^m(e^{t\mathbf{X}})_{i,p}T_t(\delta_pO). \label{eq:X_evolution}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{lem:qf-closed-evolution}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:qf-closed-evolution} 

Let $G_i(t)=T_{-t}\delta_iT_tO$. Here $T_{-t}=e^{-t\mathcal{L}^*}$ is used only as an invertible linear map, even though it is not a quantum channel. Differentiating gives
\begin{align}
    \frac{d}{dt}G_i(t)&\overset{(1)}{=}-T_{-t}\mathcal{L}^*\delta_iT_tO+T_{-t}\delta_i\mathcal{L}^* T_tO,\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{=}\sum_{r=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{i,r}T_{-t}\delta_rT_tO,\notag\\
    &\overset{(3)}{=}\sum_{r=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{i,r}G_r(t),\qquad G_i(0)=\delta_iO, \label{eq:G_ode}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ is the product rule, $(2)$ uses \cref{eq:one_quasiderivation}, and $(3)$ is the definition of $G_r$. We verify the solution explicitly by setting
\begin{align*}
    \widetilde G_i(t):=\sum_{p=1}^m(e^{t\mathbf{X}})_{i,p}\delta_pO.
\end{align*}
The derivative of the matrix exponential gives
\begin{align*}
    \frac{d}{dt}\widetilde G_i(t)&\overset{(1)}{=}\sum_{r,p=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{i,r}(e^{t\mathbf{X}})_{r,p}\delta_pO\overset{(2)}{=}\sum_{r=1}^m\mathbf{X}_{i,r}\widetilde G_r(t),\\
    \widetilde G_i(0)&\overset{(3)}{=}\sum_{p=1}^m\delta_{i,p}\delta_pO=\delta_iO,
\end{align*}
where $(1)$ uses $\frac{d}{dt}e^{t\mathbf{X}}=\mathbf{X}e^{t\mathbf{X}}$, $(2)$ is the definition of $\widetilde G_r$, $(3)$ uses $e^{0\mathbf{X}}=\mathbb{I}$. Thus $G$ and $\widetilde G$ solve \cref{eq:G_ode} with the same initial value. Uniqueness gives $G_i(t)=\widetilde G_i(t)$. Applying $T_t$ and using $T_tT_{-t}=\operatorname{id}$ yields
\begin{align*}
    \delta_iT_tO=\sum_{p=1}^m(e^{t\mathbf{X}})_{i,p}T_t(\delta_pO).
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:qf-oscillator-mixing}
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a quasifree Lindbladian and $\sigma$ a state satisfying $\mathcal{L}(\sigma)=0$. Then for every state $\rho$ and every $t\geq0$,
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1\leq m\|e^{t\mathbf{X}}\| \cdot||\rho-\sigma||_1. \label{eq:qf_general_mixing_bound}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{lem:qf-oscillator-mixing}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:qf-oscillator-mixing} 

For a real vector $v\in\mathbb R^m$, write $c(v):=\sum_pv_pc_p$ and $\delta(v):=\sum_pv_p\delta_p$. The Majorana relations give $c(v)^2=\|v\|_2^2\mathbb{I}$, so $\|c(v)\|=\|v\|_2$. By \cref{eq:dk_commutators},
\begin{align*}
    \delta(v)O&=\frac{i}{2}\Pi[c(v),O],&
    \|\delta(v)O\|&\leq\|v\|_2\|O\|.
\end{align*}
Put $A:=e^{t\mathbf X}$ and let $e_i$ be the $i$-th coordinate vector. Combining the quasiderivations in \cref{eq:X_evolution} before taking norms gives
\begin{align*}
    \delta_iT_tO&=T_t\bigl(\delta(A^Te_i)O\bigr),\\
    \|\delta_iT_tO\|&\leq\|A^Te_i\|_2\|O\|\leq\|A\|\|O\|.
\end{align*}
Here $A$ is real, and the first inequality uses contractivity of the unital completely positive map $T_t$. The second uses $\|A^Te_i\|_2\leq\|A^T\|\|e_i\|_2=\|A\|$, since $\|e_i\|_2=1$ and the Euclidean operator norm is invariant under transposition. Summing over $i$ yields
\begin{align}
    |\mkern-1mu|\mkern-1mu|T_tO|\mkern-1mu|\mkern-1mu|_{\operatorname{m}}\leq m\|e^{t\mathbf X}\|\|O\|.
    \label{eq:qf-oscillator-contraction}
\end{align}

This allows us to bound:
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1 &\overset{(1)}{=}\sup_{\|O\|\leq1}\left|\operatorname{Tr}\left[O\left(e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-\sigma\right)\right]\right|,\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{=}\sup_{\|O\|\leq1}\left|\operatorname{Tr}\left[(T_tO)(\rho-\sigma)\right]\right|,\notag\\
    &\overset{(3)}{=}\sup_{\|O\|\leq1}\inf_{z\in\mathbb C}\left|\operatorname{Tr}\left[(T_tO-z\mathbb{I})(\rho-\sigma)\right]\right|,\notag\\
    &\overset{(4)}{\leq}\|\rho -\sigma \|_1\sup_{\|O\|\leq1}\inf_{z\in\mathbb C}\left\|T_tO-z\mathbb{I}\right\|, \label{eq:qf-trace-duality}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ uses the variational definition of the trace norm $\|A\|_1=\sup_{\|O\|\leq1}\left|\operatorname{Tr}(OA)\right|$, $(2)$ uses adjointness and stationarity of $\sigma$, $(3)$ uses $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho-\sigma)=0$, and $(4)$ uses H\"older's inequality.

Finally, using \cref{eq:qf-telescoping} and then \cref{eq:qf-oscillator-contraction} we have:
\begin{align}
    \inf_{z\in\mathbb C}\left\|T_tO-z\mathbb{I}\right\|&=q(T_tO)\leq |\mkern-1mu|\mkern-1mu|T_tO|\mkern-1mu|\mkern-1mu|_{\operatorname{m}}\leq m\|e^{t\mathbf{X}}\|\|O\|,
\end{align}

which yields the desired inequality
\begin{align*}
    \|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1\leq m\|e^{t\mathbf{X}}\|\cdot ||\rho-\sigma||_1.
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:quasifree_rapid_mixing} 
  \addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{ 
    \texorpdfstring{\protect\cref*{prop:quasifree_rapid_mixing}}{Result \getrefnumber{prop:quasifree_rapid_mixing}}: Rapid mixing of quasifree fermionic Lindbladians} 

Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a quasifree fermionic Lindbladian on $m=2N$ Majoranas, and let $\mathbf{M},\mathbf{X}$ be defined in \cref{app:eq:quasifree_X}. Let $\sigma$ be a state satisfying $\mathcal{L}(\sigma)=0$. Then for every state $\rho$ and every $t\geq 0$,
\begin{align*}
    \|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1\leq m\|e^{t\mathbf{X}}\|\cdot||\rho-\sigma||_1.
\end{align*}
If $\mathbf{X}=SJS^{-1}$ is a Jordan decomposition, the largest Jordan block has size $L$, and
\begin{align*}
    \gamma(\mathbf{X}):=\min_{z\in\operatorname{spec}(\mathbf{X})}-\operatorname{Re}(z)>0,
\end{align*}
then
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1\leq m\kappa(S)e^{-t\gamma(\mathbf{X})}\left(\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}\frac{t^j}{j!}\right)\|\rho-\sigma\|_1,\qquad \kappa(S):=\|S\|\|S^{-1}\|. \notag
\end{align}
The following bound also holds:
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1\leq me^{-4t\lambda_{\min}(\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M}))}\|\rho-\sigma\|_1, \notag
\end{align}
Thus, for a family $(\mathcal{L}_N)_N$ with $\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_N$ at each size, a uniform bound $\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M})\succeq\mu\mathbb{I}$ with $\mu>0$ gives rapid mixing with constant decay rate $4\mu$.

In particular, if $\gamma(\mathbf{X})=\Omega((\log N)^{-r})$ for some fixed $r\geq0$, $\kappa(S)=\operatorname{poly}(N)$, and $L=O(1)$, then $(\mathcal{L}_N)_N$ is rapidly mixing. For $\gamma(\mathbf X)=\Omega(1)$, constant-rate rapid mixing also holds with $L=O(\log(N+1))$ and $\kappa(S)=\operatorname{poly}(N)$. The same conclusions hold if $\lambda_{\min}(\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M}))$ obeys the corresponding inverse-polylogarithmic or constant lower bound. Each condition also implies uniqueness of the stationary state.
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{prop:quasifree_rapid_mixing}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:quasifree_rapid_mixing} 

A stationary state exists because $\mathcal{L}$ is a finite-dimensional Lindbladian. The first estimate is \cref{lem:qf-oscillator-mixing}. We bound $\|e^{t\mathbf{X}}\|$ in two ways. For a Jordan block $z\mathbb{I}+N_r$ of size $r\leq L$, the matrix $N_r$ has ones on the first superdiagonal and $N_r^r=0$. Its powers have norm at most one, so
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t(z\mathbb{I}+N_r)}\|&\overset{(1)}{\leq}e^{t\operatorname{Re}(z)}\sum_{q=0}^{r-1}\frac{t^q}{q!},\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{\leq}e^{-t\gamma(\mathbf{X})}(t+1)^{r-1},\notag\\
    \|e^{t\mathbf{X}}\|&\overset{(3)}{\leq}\kappa(S)e^{-t\gamma(\mathbf{X})}\sum_{q=0}^{L-1}\frac{t^q}{q!}, \label{eq:qf-jordan-matrix}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ expands the finite exponential series and uses the triangle inequality with $||N_r||\leq1$, $(2)$ uses $\operatorname{Re}(z)\leq-\gamma(\mathbf{X})$ and compares coefficients with $(t+1)^{r-1}$, and $(3)$ takes the maximum over the Jordan blocks, with $r\leq L$, and uses $e^{t\mathbf{X}}=Se^{tJ}S^{-1}$.

For a uniform lower bound $\gamma(\mathbf X)\geq\gamma_0>0$, the inequality $e^{-at}(at)^j/j!\leq1$ with $a=\gamma_0/2$ gives
\begin{align*}
    \|e^{t\mathbf X}\|
    \leq\kappa(S)\left[\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}
        \left(\frac2{\gamma_0}\right)^j\right]e^{-\gamma_0t/2}.
\end{align*}
If $\kappa(S)=\operatorname{poly}(N)$ and $L=O(\log(N+1))$, the bracket is polynomial in $N$, proving rapid mixing with constant decay rate.

For the second estimate, $\mathbf{X}$ is real and $\mathbf{H}^T=-\mathbf{H}$, so \cref{app:eq:quasifree_X} gives $(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{X}^T)/2=-4\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M})$. Since $\|e^{tA}\|\leq\|e^{t(A+A^\dagger)/2}\|$ for every matrix $A$ and every $t\geq0$ \cite[Theorem~IX.3.1]{bhatia2013matrix}, and $\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M})$ is real symmetric,
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t\mathbf{X}}\|\leq\bigl\|e^{-4t\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M})}\bigr\|=e^{-4t\lambda_{\min}(\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M}))}. \label{eq:qf-hermitian-part-bound}
\end{align}
In particular $\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M})\succeq\mu\mathbb{I}$ with $\mu>0$ gives $\|e^{t\mathbf{X}}\|\leq e^{-4\mu t}$.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{app:cor:sum-gaussian}
Let $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{K}$ be quasifree fermionic Lindbladians on the same $m=2N$ Majoranas, with $\mathbf{M}$ matrices $\mathbf{M}_\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathbf{M}_\mathcal{K}$, and suppose that $\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M}_\mathcal{L})\succeq\mu\mathbb{I}$ for some $\mu>0$. Then $\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}$ has a unique stationary state $\sigma_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}}$, and for every state $\rho$ and every $t\geq0$,
\begin{align}
    \lVert e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K})}(\rho)-\sigma_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}}\rVert_1\leq me^{-4\mu t}\|\rho-\sigma_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}}\|_1.
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{cor:sum-gaussian}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:sum-gaussian} 

The sum $\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}$ is quasifree, with quadratic Hamiltonian $\mathbf{H}_\mathcal{L}+\mathbf{H}_\mathcal{K}$ and jump set the union of the two jump sets, so $\mathbf{M}_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}}=\mathbf{M}_\mathcal{L}+\mathbf{M}_\mathcal{K}$. Each $\mathbf{M}$ is Hermitian and positive semidefinite, and $\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M})$ is real symmetric with $v^T\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M})v=v^\dagger\mathbf{M}v\geq0$ for real $v$, so $\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M}_\mathcal{K})\succeq0$ and therefore
\begin{align*}
    \operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M}_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}})=\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M}_\mathcal{L})+\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf{M}_\mathcal{K})\succeq\mu\mathbb{I}.
\end{align*}
Every finite-dimensional Lindbladian has a stationary state. \Cref{prop:quasifree_rapid_mixing} applied to $\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}$ gives the desired result. Since the right-hand side tends to zero, applying it to two stationary states proves uniqueness. Applying this estimate at every size with the same $\mu>0$ and $m=2N$ proves the family statement in \cref{cor:sum-gaussian}.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:qf-matrix-stability}
Let $\mathcal{L},\mathcal{G}$ be quasifree Lindbladians on the same $m$ Majoranas, with single-particle matrices $\mathbf X_\mathcal{L},\mathbf X_\mathcal{G}$. Suppose that, for some $t_0>0$, $0<q<1$, and $\eta\geq0$,
\begin{align*}
    \|e^{t_0\mathbf X_\mathcal{L}}\|\leq q,\qquad
    \|\mathbf X_\mathcal{G}-\mathbf X_\mathcal{L}\|\leq\eta,\qquad
    q':=q+t_0\eta<1.
\end{align*}
Then $\mathcal{G}$ has a unique stationary state $\sigma_\mathcal{G}$, and, for every state $\rho$ and $t\geq0$,
\begin{align*}
    \|e^{t\mathcal{G}}(\rho)-\sigma_\mathcal{G}\|_1
    \leq\frac{m}{q'}\exp\left[-\frac{\log(1/q')}{t_0}t\right]\|\rho-\sigma_\mathcal{G}\|_1.
\end{align*}
For families $(\mathcal{L}_N)_N$ and $(\mathcal{G}_N)_N$ satisfying these bounds with $t_0,q,\eta$ independent of $N$, $(\mathcal{G}_N)_N$ is rapidly mixing with constant decay rate.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
The single-particle semigroup of every quasifree Lindbladian is contractive. Indeed, for $\mathbf X=-\mathbf H-4\operatorname{Re}\mathbf M$ and $v_s=e^{s\mathbf X}v$,
\begin{align}
    \frac{d}{ds}\|v_s\|_2^2
    =v_s^\dagger(\mathbf X+\mathbf X^T)v_s
    =-8v_s^\dagger\operatorname{Re}\mathbf M\,v_s\leq0.
    \label{eq:qf-ti-one-particle-contractivity}
\end{align}
Duhamel's formula therefore gives
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t\mathbf X_\mathcal{G}}-e^{t\mathbf X_\mathcal{L}}\|
    &\leq\int_0^t
    \|e^{(t-s)\mathbf X_\mathcal{G}}\|\,
    \|\mathbf X_\mathcal{G}-\mathbf X_\mathcal{L}\|\,
    \|e^{s\mathbf X_\mathcal{L}}\|\,ds
    \leq t\eta. \label{eq:qf-ti-duhamel}
\end{align}
In particular $\|e^{t_0\mathbf X_\mathcal{G}}\|\leq q'$. Write $t=jt_0+u$, with $j=\lfloor t/t_0\rfloor$ and $0\leq u<t_0$. The semigroup property and contractivity imply
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t\mathbf X_\mathcal{G}}\|
    \leq(q')^j
    \leq\frac1{q'}\exp\left[-\frac{\log(1/q')}{t_0}t\right].
    \label{eq:qf-ti-perturbed-decay}
\end{align}
A stationary state $\sigma_\mathcal{G}$ exists in finite dimension. Applying \cref{lem:qf-oscillator-mixing} proves the bound. Applying it to another stationary state and taking $t\to\infty$ proves uniqueness.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{app:prop:qf-translation-invariant-stability}
Let $(\mathcal{L}_N)_N$ be a translation-invariant quasifree Lindbladian family on periodic lattices $\Lambda_N=(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^D$, with one fermionic mode per unit cell and uniformly bounded interaction strength $s_{\mathcal{L}}$. Here $s_{\mathcal{L}}:=\sup_N\sup_{x\in\Lambda_N}\sum_{Z\ni x}\|\mathcal{L}_N^{(Z)}\|_{1\to1}<\infty$ for a decomposition $\mathcal{L}_N=\sum_{Z\subseteq\Lambda_N}\mathcal{L}_N^{(Z)}$ into quasifree Lindbladians supported on $Z$, with each norm computed on the modes in $Z$. Let $\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N}$ be its single-particle matrix. Suppose that for some $\gamma>0$, independently of $N$,
\begin{align}
    \max_{z\in\operatorname{spec}(\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N})}\operatorname{Re}z&\leq-\gamma\qquad\text{for every }N,
\end{align}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[a)] The family $(\mathcal{L}_N)_N$ is rapidly mixing with constant decay rate.
\item[b)] For every interaction-strength bound $s_{\mathcal{K}}\geq0$, there exists a constant $\varepsilon_*>0$, independent of $N$, such that, for every quasifree Lindbladian family $(\mathcal{K}_N)_N$, not necessarily translation invariant, admitting a decomposition
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{K}_N&=\sum_{Z\subseteq\Lambda_N}\mathcal{K}_N^{(Z)},
    &\sup_N\sup_{x\in\Lambda_N}\sum_{Z\ni x}\|\mathcal{K}_N^{(Z)}\|_{1\to1}&\leq s_{\mathcal{K}}, \label{app:eq:qf-ti-local-perturbation}
\end{align}
where each $\mathcal{K}_N^{(Z)}$ is a quasifree Lindbladian supported on $Z$ and each local norm is computed on the modes in $Z$, the family $(\mathcal{L}_N+\varepsilon\mathcal{K}_N)_N$ remains rapidly mixing with constant decay rate for all $0\leq\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_*$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{prop:qf-translation-invariant-stability}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:qf-translation-invariant-stability} 

The local-matrix estimate in \cref{eq:qf-ti-local-drift-bound} and the weighted-overlap argument in \cref{eq:qf-ti-weighted-overlap}, proved below for supported quasifree Lindbladian terms, apply equally to the decomposition of $\mathcal{L}_N$. They give
\begin{align*}
    \|\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N}\|&\leq s_{\mathcal{L}}\qquad\text{for every }N.
\end{align*}
The spatial Fourier transform $U_N$ is unitary and block diagonalizes the translation-invariant single-particle matrix into its two-dimensional momentum blocks:
\begin{align}
    U_N\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N}U_N^\dagger&=\bigoplus_{k\in\Lambda_N^*}\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N}(k),
    &\|e^{t\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N}}\|&=\max_{k\in\Lambda_N^*}\|e^{t\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N}(k)}\|, \label{eq:qf-ti-fourier-blocks}
\end{align}
where $\Lambda_N^*$ is the discrete momentum grid in $\mathbb T^D=[-\pi,\pi)^D$. Unitary invariance gives $\|\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N}(k)\|\leq s_{\mathcal{L}}$ for every $N$ and $k\in\Lambda_N^*$. The assumed spectral bound for $\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N}$ also holds for each of these blocks.

For every $N$ and $k\in\Lambda_N^*$, take a Schur decomposition $\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N}(k)=Q_N(k)T_N(k)Q_N(k)^\dagger$. The matrices $Q_N(k)$ are unitary, while $T_N(k)$ is a $2\times2$ upper-triangular matrix with norm at most $s_{\mathcal{L}}$ and diagonal entries with real parts at most $-\gamma$. Its off-diagonal matrix element has magnitude at most $s_{\mathcal{L}}$, so the explicit exponential gives
\begin{align}
    \|e^{tT_N(k)}\|&\leq(2+s_{\mathcal{L}}t)e^{-\gamma t}. \label{eq:qf-ti-schur-bound}
\end{align}
Indeed, the off-diagonal entry is an integral of the form $\int_0^t e^{(t-s)z_1}b e^{sz_2}\,ds$, whose magnitude is at most $s_{\mathcal{L}}t e^{-\gamma t}$. Unitary invariance and \cref{eq:qf-ti-fourier-blocks} therefore give
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N}}\|&\leq(2+s_{\mathcal{L}}t)e^{-\gamma t}\leq C_{s_{\mathcal{L}},\gamma}e^{-\gamma t/2}, \label{eq:qf-ti-one-particle-decay}
\end{align}
with $C_{s_{\mathcal{L}},\gamma}$ independent of $N$. Applying \cref{prop:quasifree_rapid_mixing}, with the linear factor $m_N=2|\Lambda_N|$ in the number of Majoranas, proves rapid mixing with constant decay rate.

We now allow the perturbation to break translation invariance. First choose a time $t_0>0$, depending only on $s_{\mathcal{L}}$ and $\gamma$, such that the right-hand side of \cref{eq:qf-ti-one-particle-decay} is at most $1/2$. Thus
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t_0\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N}}\|\leq\frac12 \qquad\text{for every }N. \label{eq:qf-ti-fixed-contraction}
\end{align}
To preserve this contraction, we bound the change in the single-particle matrix using the local strength of $\mathcal{K}_N$. For each term $\mathcal{K}_N^{(Z)}$, let $\mathbf X_{\mathcal{K}_N}^{(Z)}$ be its matrix on the $2|Z|$ Majorana labels in $Z$, extended by zero on all other labels. Additivity of the Hamiltonian and dissipative matrices gives
\begin{align*}
    \mathbf X_{\mathcal{K}_N}&:=\sum_Z\mathbf X_{\mathcal{K}_N}^{(Z)},\\
    \mathcal{L}_{\varepsilon,N}&:=\mathcal{L}_N+\varepsilon\mathcal{K}_N,
    &\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_{\varepsilon,N}}&=\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_N}+\varepsilon\mathbf X_{\mathcal{K}_N}.
\end{align*}
We first bound each local matrix, and then sum these bounds using the overlap of the supports.

Fix $Z$, and list its Majoranas as $c_{Z,1},\ldots,c_{Z,2|Z|}$. Define the parity operator on these modes and, for a real vector $v\in\mathbb R^{2|Z|}$, the observable
\begin{align*}
    \Pi_Z&:=(-i)^{|Z|}c_{Z,1}\cdots c_{Z,2|Z|},
    &\widetilde c_Z(v)&:=i\Pi_Z\sum_{j=1}^{2|Z|}v_jc_{Z,j}.
\end{align*}
These are the local versions of \cref{eq:qf-parity-dressing}. The operators $i\Pi_Zc_{Z,j}$ are Hermitian and satisfy the Majorana relations, so
\begin{align*}
    \widetilde c_Z(v)^2&=\|v\|_2^2\mathbb{I}_Z,
    &\|\widetilde c_Z(v)\|&=\|v\|_2.
\end{align*}
Since $\widetilde c_Z(v)$ is linear in the dressed Majoranas, $\delta_i\delta_j\widetilde c_Z(v)=0$ for all $i,j$. Thus \cref{eq:qf_adjoint_quasiderivations}, applied on $Z$, reduces to
\begin{align*}
    (\mathcal{K}_N^{(Z)})^*(\widetilde c_Z(v))&=\widetilde c_Z(\mathbf X_{\mathcal{K}_N}^{(Z)}v).
\end{align*}
Taking norms now relates the local matrix to the local generator:
\begin{align*}
    \|\mathbf X_{\mathcal{K}_N}^{(Z)}v\|_2
    &=\|(\mathcal{K}_N^{(Z)})^*(\widetilde c_Z(v))\|\\
    &\leq\|(\mathcal{K}_N^{(Z)})^*\|_{\infty\to\infty}\|\widetilde c_Z(v)\|\\
    &=\|\mathcal{K}_N^{(Z)}\|_{1\to1}\|v\|_2.
\end{align*}
The last equality uses trace--operator norm duality. Since $\mathbf X_{\mathcal{K}_N}^{(Z)}$ is real, its operator norm is attained on real vectors. Taking the supremum over real unit vectors therefore gives
\begin{align}
    \|\mathbf X_{\mathcal{K}_N}^{(Z)}\|&\leq\|\mathcal{K}_N^{(Z)}\|_{1\to1}. \label{eq:qf-ti-local-drift-bound}
\end{align}
For a vector $u$, let $u_Z$ be its restriction to the Majorana labels in $Z$ and put $w_Z:=\|\mathcal{K}_N^{(Z)}\|_{1\to1}$. The local-strength bound in \cref{app:eq:qf-ti-local-perturbation} gives
\begin{align}
    \sum_Zw_Z\|u_Z\|_2^2
    &=\sum_i|u_i|^2\sum_{Z\ni x_i}w_Z
    \leq s_{\mathcal{K}}\|u\|_2^2, \label{eq:qf-ti-weighted-overlap}
\end{align}
where $x_i$ is the site of Majorana label $i$. Hence, for arbitrary vectors $u,v$,
\begin{align}
    |u^\dagger\mathbf X_{\mathcal{K}_N}v|
    &\leq\sum_Zw_Z\|u_Z\|_2\|v_Z\|_2 \notag\\
    &\leq\left(\sum_Zw_Z\|u_Z\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}
    \left(\sum_Zw_Z\|v_Z\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}\notag\\
    &\leq s_{\mathcal{K}}\|u\|_2\|v\|_2, \notag
\end{align}
Taking the supremum over unit vectors proves the size-independent estimate
\begin{align}
    \|\mathbf X_{\mathcal{K}_N}\|\leq s_{\mathcal{K}}. \label{eq:qf-ti-full-perturbation}
\end{align}

Apply \cref{lem:qf-matrix-stability} with $\mathcal{G}=\mathcal{L}_{\varepsilon,N}$, $q=1/2$, and $\eta=\varepsilon s_{\mathcal{K}}$. Choose $\varepsilon_*>0$ such that $t_0\varepsilon_*s_{\mathcal{K}}\leq1/4$. This choice depends only on $s_{\mathcal{L}},\gamma,s_{\mathcal{K}}$, so it works for every perturbation family satisfying the prescribed bound. Then \cref{eq:qf-ti-fixed-contraction,eq:qf-ti-full-perturbation} and the Duhamel estimate in the lemma give, for $0\leq\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_*$,
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t_0\mathbf X_{\mathcal{L}_{\varepsilon,N}}}\|\leq\frac34. \label{eq:qf-ti-perturbed-contraction}
\end{align}
Iterating this contraction as in the lemma gives a unique stationary state $\sigma_{\varepsilon,N}$ and
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t\mathcal{L}_{\varepsilon,N}}(\rho)-\sigma_{\varepsilon,N}\|_1
    &\leq\frac43m_N\exp\left[-\frac{\log(4/3)}{t_0}t\right]\|\rho-\sigma_{\varepsilon,N}\|_1, \label{eq:qf-ti-perturbed-mixing}
\end{align}
where $m_N=2|\Lambda_N|$. The prefactor is linear in the system size and the decay rate is independent of $N$, completing the proof.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- corollary-10: body_md -->
\label{cor:qf-uniform-dissipation} 
  \addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{ 
    \texorpdfstring{\protect\cref*{cor:qf-uniform-dissipation}}{Result \getrefnumber{cor:qf-uniform-dissipation}}: Uniform rapid mixing under uniform dissipation} 

Let $(\mathcal{L}_N)_N$ be a family of quasifree fermionic Lindbladians with one fermionic mode per site. Suppose that there exist $\mu,R_0>0$, independent of the system size, such that every restriction to $A=b_x(R)$ with $x\in\Lambda$ and $R\geq R_0$ satisfies
\begin{align*}
    \operatorname{Re}(\mathbf M_A)\succeq\mu\mathbb{I}.
\end{align*}
Then $\mathcal{L}_A$ has a unique stationary state $\sigma_{\mathcal{L}_A}$, and for every state $\rho$ on $A$ and every $t\geq0$,
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t\mathcal{L}_A}(\rho)-\sigma_{\mathcal{L}_A}\|_1\leq m_Ae^{-4\mu t}\|\rho-\sigma_{\mathcal{L}_A}\|_1, \label{app:eq:qf-uniform-dissipation}
\end{align}
where $m_A=2|A|$ is the number of Majoranas in $A$. Thus the family is uniformly rapidly mixing with constant decay rate. The same bound holds with $\sigma_{\mathcal{L}_A+\mathcal{K}_A}$ for $\mathcal{L}_A+\mathcal{K}_A$ whenever $(\mathcal{K}_N)_N$ is a quasifree Lindbladian family on the same modes and $\mathcal{K}_A$ retains its Hamiltonian terms and jumps supported entirely on $A$.
<!-- end corollary-10 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{cor:qf-uniform-dissipation}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:qf-uniform-dissipation} 

Fix $A=b_x(R)$ with $R\geq R_0$. Every finite-dimensional Lindbladian has a stationary state; let $\sigma_{\mathcal{L}_A}$ be one for $\mathcal{L}_A$.

Applying \cref{prop:quasifree_rapid_mixing} to this stationary state gives
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t\mathcal{L}_A}(\rho)-\sigma_{\mathcal{L}_A}\|_1 &\overset{(1)}{\leq}m_Ae^{-4t\lambda_{\min}(\operatorname{Re}\mathbf M_A)}\|\rho-\sigma_{\mathcal{L}_A}\|_1,\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{\leq}m_Ae^{-4\mu t}\|\rho-\sigma_{\mathcal{L}_A}\|_1,\notag\\
    &\overset{(3)}{=}2|A|e^{-4\mu t}\|\rho-\sigma_{\mathcal{L}_A}\|_1, \notag
\end{align}
where $(1)$ is the quasifree mixing estimate, $(2)$ uses the uniform lower bound on $\operatorname{Re}\mathbf M_A$, and $(3)$ uses $m_A=2|A|$. Applying the bound to another stationary state and taking $t\to\infty$ proves uniqueness. The prefactor $2|A|$ is linear in the number of sites, and the decay rate $4\mu$ is independent of $A$ and $\Lambda$, proving uniform rapid mixing with constant decay rate.

For an addition, the retained jump sets give $\mathbf M_{\mathcal{L}_A+\mathcal{K}_A}=\mathbf M_{\mathcal{L}_A}+\mathbf M_{\mathcal{K}_A}$. Since $\operatorname{Re}\mathbf M_{\mathcal{K}_A}\succeq0$, the same lower bound $\operatorname{Re}\mathbf M_{\mathcal{L}_A+\mathcal{K}_A}\succeq\mu\mathbb{I}$ holds. The preceding argument applied to $\mathcal{L}_A+\mathcal{K}_A$ proves the remaining claim.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:infinite-time-limit}
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a Lindbladian on a finite-dimensional $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$. The infinite-time limit $P_\mathcal{L}=\lim_{t\to\infty}e^{t\mathcal{L}}$, understood pointwise as $P_\mathcal{L}(X)=\lim_{t\to\infty}e^{t\mathcal{L}}(X)$ for every $X\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$, exists if and only if $\mathcal{L}$ has no nonzero purely imaginary eigenvalue, i.e.\ $\operatorname{spec}(\mathcal{L})\cap i\mathbb{R}=\{0\}$.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{lem:infinite-time-limit}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:infinite-time-limit} 

The spectral condition is necessary: if $\mathcal{L} X=i\omega X$ with $\omega\neq0$ and $X\neq0$, then $e^{t\mathcal{L}}(X)=e^{i\omega t}X$ oscillates, so the limit fails to exist already at this single $X$. It is also sufficient: let $\operatorname{spec}(\mathcal{L})\cap i\mathbb{R}=\{0\}$. Every eigenvalue of a Lindbladian has $\operatorname{Re}\lambda\le0$, so by assumption every $\lambda\neq0$ has $\operatorname{Re}\lambda<0$.

We first show $\ker\mathcal{L}^2=\ker\mathcal{L}$. If $\mathcal{L}^2X=0$ then $Y:=\mathcal{L} X$ lies in $\ker\mathcal{L}$, so the exponential series terminates after two terms: $e^{t\mathcal{L}}(X)=X+tY$. Each $e^{t\mathcal{L}}$ is a channel and hence does not increase trace distance, $\|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(A)-e^{t\mathcal{L}}(B)\|_1\le\|A-B\|_1$, which for $B=0$ says that no trajectory can grow; this forces $Y=\mathcal{L} X=0$. Consequently $\ker\mathcal{L}\cap\operatorname{ran}\mathcal{L}=\{0\}$: an element $Y=\mathcal{L} X$ of the intersection satisfies $\mathcal{L}^2X=\mathcal{L} Y=0$, hence $X\in\ker\mathcal{L}^2=\ker\mathcal{L}$ and $Y=\mathcal{L} X=0$. Together with $\dim\ker\mathcal{L}+\dim\operatorname{ran}\mathcal{L}=\dim\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ this gives the decomposition
\begin{align}
    &\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})=\ker\mathcal{L}\oplus\operatorname{ran}\mathcal{L} ,
\end{align}
in which $\operatorname{ran}\mathcal{L}$ is invariant under $e^{t\mathcal{L}}$ because $\mathcal{L}$ commutes with it. Split $X\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ accordingly as $X=X_0+X_1$. The kernel part stays fixed, $e^{t\mathcal{L}}(X_0)=X_0$, while the remainder decays: the restriction of $\mathcal{L}$ to $\operatorname{ran}\mathcal{L}$ is invertible, so its eigenvalues are among the $\lambda\neq0$ and have $\operatorname{Re}\lambda<0$, whence $e^{t\mathcal{L}}(X_1)\to0$. Therefore $e^{t\mathcal{L}}(X)\to X_0$ for every $X$, i.e. the pointwise limit exists.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:commuting-sum}\label{app:lem:commuting-sum}
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{K}$ be commuting Lindbladians acting on $\mathcal{D}_1(\mathcal{H})$ each with a well-defined infinite-time limit. Then, for any $\rho\in\mathcal{D}_1(\mathcal{H})$
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K})}(\rho)-P_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}}(\rho)\|_1 \leq \|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-P_{\mathcal{L}}(\rho)\|_1 +\|e^{t\mathcal{K}}(\rho)-P_{\mathcal{K}}(\rho)\|_1,
\end{align}
and the mixing times satisfy:
\begin{align}
    \tau_{\operatorname{mix}}^{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}}(\delta) \leq \max\{\tau_{\operatorname{mix}}^{\mathcal{L}}(\delta/2),\tau_{\operatorname{mix}}^{\mathcal{K}}(\delta/2)\} .
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{lem:commuting-sum}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:commuting-sum} 

We follow the telescoping proof of \cite[Theorem~6]{KastoryanoWolf2012}, keeping the initial state fixed instead of taking the supremum over states. Since $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{K}$ commute we have
\begin{align}
    e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K})} = e^{t\mathcal{L}} \circ e^{t\mathcal{K}} = e^{t\mathcal{K}} \circ e^{t\mathcal{L}} \quad \mathrm{and} \quad P_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}} = P_{\mathcal{L}} \circ P_{\mathcal{K}} = P_{\mathcal{K}} \circ P_{\mathcal{L}} .
\end{align}
Then
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K})} (\rho) - P_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}} (\rho) \|_1 &\overset{(1)}{\leq} \|e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K})} (\rho) -  e^{t\mathcal{K}} (P_{\mathcal{L}}(\rho) )\|_1+\| e^{t\mathcal{K}}(  P_{\mathcal{L}}(\rho) )  - P_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}} (\rho) \|_1,\notag\\
    &\overset{(2)}{=}\|e^{t\mathcal{K}}(e^{t\mathcal{L}} (\rho) -P_{\mathcal{L}}  (\rho ) )\|_1+\| P_{\mathcal{L}} (e^{t\mathcal{K}} (\rho)  - P_{\mathcal{K}} (\rho) ) \|_1,\notag\\
    &\overset{(3)}{\leq} \|e^{t\mathcal{L}} (\rho) -P_{\mathcal{L}}  (\rho) \|_1+\|e^{t\mathcal{K}} (\rho)  - P_{\mathcal{K}} (\rho) \|_1,   \label{eq:tracenormbound:split}
\end{align}
where $(1)$ uses the triangle inequality, $(2)$  that $[P_{\mathcal{L}}, e^{t \mathcal{K}}] = 0$ and $(3)$ that the trace norm is contractive under the quantum channels $e^{t\mathcal{K}},P_\mathcal{L}$. For any time strictly larger than the maximum of the two mixing times at error $\delta/2$, both terms are at most $\delta/2$. Taking the infimum gives the mixing-time bound.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{app:lem:commuting-unique-stationary}
Let $\mathcal{L},\mathcal{K}$ be commuting Lindbladians and suppose that $\mathcal{L}$ has a unique stationary state $\sigma$ and a well-defined infinite-time limit. Then $\mathcal{K}(\sigma)=0$, $\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}$ has the unique stationary state $\sigma$, and, for every $\rho\in\mathcal{D}_1(\mathcal{H})$ and $t\ge0$,
\begin{align*}
    \|e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K})}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1\le \|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1.
\end{align*}
In particular, every rapid-mixing bound for $\mathcal{L}$ is inherited by $\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}$.
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{lem:commuting-unique-stationary}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:commuting-unique-stationary} 

For every $s\geq0$, commutativity gives
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{L}(e^{s\mathcal{K}}(\sigma))=e^{s\mathcal{K}}(\mathcal{L}(\sigma))=0.
\end{align*}
The state $e^{s\mathcal{K}}(\sigma)$ is therefore stationary for $\mathcal{L}$, so uniqueness gives $e^{s\mathcal{K}}(\sigma)=\sigma$. Differentiating at $s=0$ yields $\mathcal{K}(\sigma)=0$. Therefore $e^{t\mathcal{K}}(\sigma)=\sigma$, and
\begin{align*}
    \|e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K})}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1
    &=\|e^{t\mathcal{K}}(e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho))-e^{t\mathcal{K}}(\sigma)\|_1\\
    &\le \|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1
\end{align*}
by trace-norm contractivity of $e^{t\mathcal{K}}$. The right-hand side tends to zero because $P_\mathcal{L}(\rho)$ is a stationary state of $\mathcal{L}$ and therefore equals $\sigma$. Thus every initial state converges to $\sigma$ under $\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}$, which also proves uniqueness of its stationary state.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{app:lem:commuting-kernel}
Let $\mathcal{L},\mathcal{K}$ be commuting Lindbladians, suppose that $P_\mathcal{L}=\lim_{t\to\infty}e^{t\mathcal{L}}$ exists, and assume $\ker(\mathcal{L})\subseteq\ker(\mathcal{K})$. Then $P_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}}$ exists and equals $P_\mathcal{L}$, and for all $\rho\in\mathcal{D}_1(\mathcal{H})$ and all $t\ge0$,
\begin{align*}
    \|e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K})}(\rho)-P_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}}(\rho)\|_1\le \|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-P_\mathcal{L}(\rho)\|_1.
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{lem:commuting-kernel}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:commuting-kernel} 

Kernel inclusion gives $\mathcal{K} P_\mathcal{L}=0$, hence $e^{t\mathcal{K}}P_\mathcal{L}=P_\mathcal{L}$. Using commutativity and trace-norm contractivity, we obtain
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K})}(\rho)-P_\mathcal{L}(\rho)\|_1
    &=\|e^{t\mathcal{K}}(e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-P_\mathcal{L}(\rho))\|_1,\notag\\
    &\leq\|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-P_\mathcal{L}(\rho)\|_1.\label{eq:commuting-kernel-contraction}
\end{align}
The right-hand side tends to zero, so the infinite-time limit of the sum exists and equals $P_\mathcal{L}$. This proves the stated inequality.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:reset}
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a Lindbladian with a fixed point $\sigma\in\mathcal{D}_1(\mathcal{H})$, not necessarily full rank, and let $\mathcal{K}$ be the reset Lindbladian to $\sigma$,
\begin{align}
    \label{eq:reset} &\mathcal{K}(A)=\operatorname{Tr}[A]\,\sigma-A ,
\end{align}
which satisfies $\|\mathcal{K}\|_{1\to1}\le2$, $\ker\mathcal{K}=\mathbb{C}\sigma$ and $P_\mathcal{K}(A)=\operatorname{Tr}[A]\,\sigma$. Then $[\mathcal{L},\mathcal{K}]=0$ and, for every $\varepsilon>0$, every $\rho\in\mathcal{D}_1(\mathcal{H})$ and every $t\ge0$,
\begin{align}
    \label{eq:resetdecay} &\|e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\varepsilon\mathcal{K})}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1\le e^{-\varepsilon t}\|\rho-\sigma\|_1 ,
\end{align}
irrespective of the mixing behaviour of $\mathcal{L}$. In particular $\mathcal{L}+\varepsilon\mathcal{K}$ has the well-defined infinite-time limit $P_{\mathcal{L}+\varepsilon\mathcal{K}}(A)=\operatorname{Tr}[A]\,\sigma$ and its only fixed point among the states is $\sigma$.
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{lem:reset}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:reset} 

Let $\sigma=\sum_k p_k|k\rangle\langle k|$ and let $\{|j\rangle\}$ be any orthonormal basis. The jump operators $L_{kj}=\sqrt{p_k}\,|k\rangle\langle j|$ satisfy $\sum_{k,j}L_{kj}AL_{kj}^\dagger=\operatorname{Tr}[A]\,\sigma$ and $\sum_{k,j}L_{kj}^\dagger L_{kj}=\mathbf 1$, so the GKSL generator they define with vanishing Hamiltonian is exactly \cref{eq:reset}; and $\|\mathcal{K}(A)\|_1\le|\operatorname{Tr} A|+\|A\|_1\le2\|A\|_1$.

Write $\mathcal{R}(A)=\operatorname{Tr}[A]\,\sigma$, so that $\mathcal{K}=\mathcal{R}-\mathrm{id}$ with $\mathcal{R}^2=\mathcal{R}$, and $e^{t\mathcal{L}}\circ\mathcal{R}=\mathcal{R}$ because $e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\sigma)=\sigma$. The two generators commute,
\begin{align}
    &\mathcal{L}\mathcal{K}(A)=\operatorname{Tr}[A]\,\mathcal{L}(\sigma)-\mathcal{L}(A)=-\mathcal{L}(A)=\operatorname{Tr}[\mathcal{L}(A)]\,\sigma-\mathcal{L}(A)=\mathcal{K}\mathcal{L}(A) ,
\end{align}
by $\mathcal{L}(\sigma)=0$ and the fact that $\mathcal{L}$ is trace-annihilating, so with $e^{s\mathcal{K}}=e^{-s}e^{s\mathcal{R}}=e^{-s}\,\mathrm{id}+(1-e^{-s})\,\mathcal{R}$,
\begin{align}
    \label{eq:resetsemigroup} &e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\varepsilon\mathcal{K})}=e^{t\mathcal{L}}\circ e^{\varepsilon t\mathcal{K}} =e^{-\varepsilon t}\,e^{t\mathcal{L}}+(1-e^{-\varepsilon t})\,\mathcal{R},
\end{align}
where the displayed form of $e^{s\mathcal{K}}$ already gives $P_\mathcal{K}=\mathcal{R}$, while $\mathcal{K}(A)=0$ forces $A=\operatorname{Tr}[A]\,\sigma$, i.e.\ $\ker\mathcal{K}=\mathbb{C}\sigma$. Since $\|e^{t\mathcal{L}}\|_{1\to1}\le1$, the first term of \cref{eq:resetsemigroup} vanishes as $t\to\infty$, so $e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\varepsilon\mathcal{K})}\to\mathcal{R}$ and a state fixed by the semigroup equals $\mathcal{R}(\rho)=\sigma$. Applied to a state, \cref{eq:resetsemigroup} yields
\begin{align}
    \|e^{t(\mathcal{L}+\varepsilon\mathcal{K})}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1& =e^{-\varepsilon t}\|e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho)-\sigma\|_1\le e^{-\varepsilon t}\|\rho-\sigma\|_1 ,
\end{align}
the equality because $\mathcal{R}(\rho)=\sigma$ cancels the second term, and the bound by stationarity of $\sigma$ and trace-norm contractivity of $e^{t\mathcal{L}}$.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{app:thm:CE}
Assume $e^{t\mathcal{L}}$ has a full-rank invariant state $\sigma$. Then there is a unique conditional expectation $E^*_\mathcal{L}:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})\to\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L})$ with $E_\mathcal{L}(\sigma)=\sigma$, and for every $X\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$,
\begin{align*}
    \lim_{t\to+\infty}e^{t\mathcal{L}^*}(X-E^*_\mathcal{L}[X])=0, \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \lim_{t\to+\infty}e^{t\mathcal{L}}(\rho-E_\mathcal{L}(\rho))=0\quad\forall\rho\in\mathcal{D}_1(\mathcal{H}).
\end{align*}
If $\mathcal{L}$ has no nonzero purely imaginary eigenvalues, then $E_\mathcal{L}=P_\mathcal{L}$.
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{thm:CE}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:CE} 

The existence and uniqueness of the conditional expectation, and the decay of the complementary component, follow from \cite[Proposition~8]{carbone2013decoherence} and \cite[Theorem~19]{carbone2015environment}. Suppose in addition that $\mathcal{L}$ has no nonzero purely imaginary eigenvalues. The dual evolution on the finite-dimensional decoherence-free algebra $\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L})$ is a group of $*$-automorphisms, whose generator is diagonalizable with purely imaginary spectrum. The absence of nonzero purely imaginary eigenvalues therefore makes this evolution the identity, so $e^{t\mathcal{L}^*}(E_\mathcal{L}^*[X])=E_\mathcal{L}^*[X]$. By linearity and the decay statement above,
\begin{align*}
    e^{t\mathcal{L}^*}(X)
    &=e^{t\mathcal{L}^*}(E_\mathcal{L}^*[X])+e^{t\mathcal{L}^*}(X-E_\mathcal{L}^*[X])\\
    &=E_\mathcal{L}^*[X]+e^{t\mathcal{L}^*}(X-E_\mathcal{L}^*[X])\longrightarrow E_\mathcal{L}^*[X].
\end{align*}
Taking preduals gives $P_\mathcal{L}=E_\mathcal{L}$.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:chainrule}
Let $E^*:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})\to\mathcal{N}$ be a conditional expectation onto a unital $*$-subalgebra $\mathcal{N}\subseteq\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$, and let $E$ be its state predual. Let $\sigma\in\mathcal{D}_1(\mathcal{H})$ satisfy $E(\sigma)=\sigma$. Then for every $\rho\in\mathcal{D}_1(\mathcal{H})$,
\begin{align}
    \label{eq:chainrule} D(\rho\|\sigma)=D(\rho\|E(\rho))+D(E(\rho)\|\sigma).
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
\label{prop:swap_fixpoint}
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a Lindbladian with a well-defined infinite-time limit, and let $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in\mathcal{D}_1(\mathcal{H})$ be full-rank states in its kernel. Then $\log\sigma_1-\log\sigma_2\in\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L})=\ker\mathcal{L}^*$, so in particular
\begin{align}
    &E^*_\mathcal{L}(\log\sigma_1-\log\sigma_2)=\log\sigma_1-\log\sigma_2,
\end{align}
and, for all $\rho\in\mathcal{D}_1(\mathcal{H})$,
\begin{align}
    \label{eq:swap} \operatorname{Tr}[\mathcal{L}(\rho)(\log\sigma_1-\log\sigma_2)]=0.
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{prop:swap_fixpoint}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:swap_fixpoint} 

On a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, the Hilbert space and decoherence-free subalgebra $\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L})$ can be written, up to unitary equivalence, as \cite{kadison1986fundamentals}:
\begin{align}
    &\mathcal{H} = \bigoplus_{i\in I} \mathcal{H}^{(1)}_i \otimes \mathcal{H}_i^{(2)},\quad \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L}) = \bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_i^{(1)})\otimes \mathbb{I}_{\mathcal{H}_i^{(2)}},
\end{align}
and there is a family of density operators $\{\tau_i:i\in I\}$ such that for every full-rank state $\rho$:
\begin{align}
    &E_\mathcal{L}(\rho) = \bigoplus_{i\in I}\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal{H}_i^{(2)}}(P_i \rho P_i)\otimes \tau_i,
\end{align}
where for each $i$, $P_i$ is the projection onto $\mathcal{H}_i^{(1)}\otimes \mathcal{H}_i^{(2)}$; see \cite[Eq.~(2.10)]{BR2022}, originally proven in \cite{deschamps2016structure}; note that \cite{BR2022} writes $E_\mathcal{N}$ for the map on observables and $E_{\mathcal{N}*}$ for its predual, the opposite of the convention used here. Since $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in\ker\mathcal{L}$ and $E_\mathcal{L}$ acts as the identity there, we can thus write the fixed points as:
\begin{align}
    \sigma_j&= E_\mathcal{L}(\sigma_j)=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\tilde{\sigma}_{j,i}\otimes \tau_i, \text{ where }\tilde{\sigma}_{j,i} := \operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal{H}_i^{(2)}}(P_i \sigma_{j} P_i), \quad j=1,2,
\end{align}
with the \emph{same} family $\{\tau_i\}$ for both $j$, and with $\tilde{\sigma}_{j,i},\tau_i>0$ because $\sigma_j$ is full rank. Now using $\log(A\otimes B)=\log A\otimes\mathbb{I}+\mathbb{I}\otimes\log B$, we obtain:
\begin{align}
    \log\sigma_1-\log\sigma_2&=\bigoplus_i\log\tilde{\sigma}_{1,i}\otimes\mathbb{I}_{\mathcal{H}_i^{(2)}}+\bigoplus_i\mathbb{I}_{\mathcal{H}_i^{(1)}}\otimes \log\tau_{i}-\bigoplus_i\log\tilde{\sigma}_{2,i}\otimes\mathbb{I}_{\mathcal{H}_i^{(2)}}-\bigoplus_i\mathbb{I}_{\mathcal{H}_i^{(1)}}\otimes \log\tau_{i} ,\notag\\
    &=\bigoplus_i\bigl(\log\tilde{\sigma}_{1,i}-\log\tilde{\sigma}_{2,i}\bigr)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{\mathcal{H}_i^{(2)}} \ \in\ \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L})=\ker\mathcal{L}^* = \operatorname{ran}E_\mathcal{L}^*, \label{eq:loglogker}
\end{align}
since the cross terms cancel, the equalities of algebras being \cref{eq:ranE}; this yields the first claim. The second claim is:
\begin{align}
    &\operatorname{Tr}[\mathcal{L}(\rho)(\log\sigma_1-\log\sigma_2)] \overset{(1)}{=}\operatorname{Tr}[\rho\,\mathcal{L}^*(\log\sigma_1-\log\sigma_2)]\overset{(2)}{=}0,
\end{align}
where $(1)$ uses the Hilbert-Schmidt adjoint and $(2)$ uses \cref{eq:loglogker}.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:EP-additive}
Let $\mathcal{L},\mathcal{K}$ be Lindbladians such that $\mathcal{L},\mathcal{K}$ and $\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}$ have well-defined infinite-time limits, and let $\sigma$ be a full-rank state in $\ker\mathcal{L}\cap\ker\mathcal{K}$. Then, for every $\rho\succ0$, the states $E_\mathcal{L}(\rho),E_\mathcal{K}(\rho),E_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}}(\rho)$ are full rank and the entropy productions are additive,
\begin{align}
    \label{eq:EP-additive} &\operatorname{EP}_{\mathcal{L}}(\rho)+\operatorname{EP}_{\mathcal{K}}(\rho)=\operatorname{EP}_{\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}}(\rho) .
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
\renewcommand{\getrefnumber{#1}}{\getrefnumber{lem:EP-additive}} 
  \refstepcounter{proof} 
  \label{proof:EP-additive} 

By linearity $\sigma\in\ker(\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K})$, so $\sigma$ is a full-rank state in $\ker\mathcal{G}$ for each $\mathcal{G}\in\{\mathcal{L},\mathcal{K},\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{K}\}$. With $c = \lambda_{\min}(\rho)/\lambda_{\max}(\sigma)$,
\begin{align}
